content.title: 3 ways to watch March Madness 2026 for free without cable; StreamEast alternatives for NCAA tournament games
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation. By Tim Brown | The Oregonian/OregonLive The NCAA men’s college basketball tournament heats up with the Round of 64 tipping off today and continuing on through Friday. If you don’t already have cable, here’s a look at which streaming services will have every game and the best ways to watch March Madness with our updated streaming guide for 2026. Get DIRECTV free trial What are the best streaming services to watch March Madness in 2026? With popular free live streaming service StreamEast now taken down for good, fans are scrambling to find ways to watch March Madness for free. There are multiple games taking place at the same time during the Round of 64, and with that comes confusion about which streaming services will have every game broadcast. If you don’t have cable and just want the cheapest possible way to watch March Madness this year, we’ve ranked all the best options. The best option : You can watch every first and second round game live for free with DIRECTV (free trial). DIRECTV is expensive after the free trial ends, but it will have every game of the tournament in one place. Sling is the second best way to watch every NCAA tournament game (costs under $25 for the first month) except those being broadcast on CBS. If you don’t have one already, you can get a HDTV antenna to pair with your Sling subscription in order to get the games being broadcast on your local CBS affiliate. Another way to see all games broadcast live on CBS is by signing up for Paramount+ . This way you will be able to watch every game broadcast on CBS up through the Elite Eight. The service costs just $12.99/month and you can use it to watch on your smart TV, phone, or tablet. For basketball fans who already have cable and just need a good way to watch games on their phone or tablet: You can use your login information to watch every NCAA Tournament game live through the March Madness Live app when you sign in with your cable provider login information.
